methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $44M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Beyond Aero, a Series A-stage transportation company founded by Eloa Guillotin, Hugo Tarlé, and Valentin Chomel, has raised $44M to date. The relevant peer universe comprises 8 private companies in the transportation sector, including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Pipedream, and FleetZero. No public transportation comparables were identified.

The stage-progression method is the applicable triangulation approach, given insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage peers within the transportation cohort to support a peer-median valuation. Using total capital raised of $44M as a proxy baseline and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A progression yields an implied valuation of $88M. The peer-median method was not executable; while 3 same-sector peers exist, none met the narrow filters of stage alignment, adjacent-stage proximity, or similar valuation-tier clustering—a 3+ datapoint threshold is required to mitigate survivorship and heterogeneity bias.

The triangulated range is $75M to $101M, with a median of $88M, supported by a single quantitative method. Key uncertainties include the absence of granular Series A–stage comp data in transportation, which limits validation of the 2.0x multiplier for this specific sector. The $88M midpoint should be treated as preliminary pending access to tighter peer financials or evidence of market comparables with closer stage and sector alignment.
